scenes.headline: How A.X-K2 reads only 2,048 tokens per query
scenes.sub: SK Telecom's 688B-parameter MoE: sparse gated attention, trained natively in FP8.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Jingle! A.X-K2 is a big Korean mixture of experts. Here's how its attention reads a fraction of the context.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: A lightweight indexer keeps the top 2,048 tokens for each query, and gated latent attention reads only those. The gate makes the indexer's job easier.
scenes.say: A small indexer keeps the top two thousand and forty-eight tokens per query, and gated latent attention reads only those.

scenes.title: Inside one Sparse Gated Attention block

steps.say: Hidden states enter GatedNorm: one input-dependent gate after the norm, which suppresses massive activations.
A lightweight indexer scores every cached key and keeps the top two thousand and forty-eight, one token at a time.
Latent attention then runs over just that selected set, not the whole cache.
A head-specific output gate scales the result before the output projection, damping attention sinks.

scenes.title: Why the gate helps the indexer

left.title: Ungated softmax
items: Mass piles onto a few sink tokens
An imitating indexer spends budget re-finding sinks
left.say: Plain softmax dumps probability onto a few sink tokens. An indexer imitating that would spend budget re-discovering the sinks.

right.title: Gated from pretraining on
items: The output gate suppresses sink mass
The indexer learns, by KL, from cleaner attention
right.say: The gate suppresses sinks all through pretraining, so the indexer, which imitates gated attention, spends its budget on relevant tokens.

scenes.title: LongBench, before and after sparsity
scenes.say: The cost: on LongBench, sixty-two point eight before sparsity, sixty-two point nine nine after. Slightly better, not worse.

items.say: The model trains in eight-bit floating point from the first optimizer step, forward and backward.
In reinforcement learning, trainer and rollout must share one FP8 recipe. A token-level fix couldn't stop the collapse.
Stepping further down to four-bit experts costs a couple of points at most.

scenes.text: Gating is the common thread: it cleans what the indexer imitates, and tames the outliers that wreck FP8.

recap: An indexer picks 2,048 tokens; gated MLA reads them
Trained natively in FP8, experts served in NVFP4
scenes.say: To recap: pick the tokens, gate the output, and train in FP8 from the first step.
